role: run D2 of docs/reviews/round3/synthesis.md section 6: replicate the retrieval acceptance shift on fresh, label-clean BANKING77-OOS items with a clean pool, and test three candidate causes of the difference between BANKING77-OOS and CLINC single-domain
what_was_seen_before_writing: All results of run D and the Jev re-run, including the post hoc leak-free analyses (docs/posthoc-round3b.md): retrieval lowers held-out rejection on BANKING77-OOS for five models (14-38 points on leak-free items) but not on CLINC single-domain; with the leak removed, retrieval closeness no longer distinguishes the splits (dense AUROC 0.90 vs 0.91). Counts of fresh label-clean validation items were computed while writing; no system has been run on them.

items.rule: only validation-split items whose normalised text appears in no earlier session, no earlier dev set and no earlier experiment's items, and whose label agrees with the original dataset (BANKING77-OOS against legacy-datasets/banking77, CLINC single-domain against clinc_oos); checked at build time and frozen with a hash

banking77_oos.in_scope: 500 drawn with the seed from the 1,063 fresh label-clean in-scope validation utterances (50 intents)
banking77_oos.held_out: all 406 fresh label-clean id-oos validation utterances (23 held-out intents)
banking77_oos.pool: the 5,905 training rows minus every row whose label disagrees with the original Banking77 label (366 rows; artifacts/posthoc/b77oos_label_audit.json), so no held-out intent is in the pool

clinc_single_domain.in_scope: the 500 validation utterances of each domain (banking, credit_cards)
clinc_single_domain.held_out: the 300 id-oos validation utterances of each domain after the first 100 (the first 100 served as specialist dev items in run D); 4 held-out intents per domain
clinc_single_domain.pool: each domain's 500 training utterances; for the pooled prompt, both domains' 1,000

clinc_single_domain.retrieval_10: the domain's own 10 options, retrieval from that domain's pool (as run D)

deepseek-v4-pro.precision: fp8 (StreamLake); originally Parasail fp8, see amendment_2026-10-16_deepseek_host

H1_replication.statement: on fresh label-clean BANKING77-OOS items with a clean pool, held-out rejection is lower with retrieval than zero-shot
H1_replication.replicates_if: significant for at least 4 of 5 models, all in the same direction

H2_relevance.statement: random in-scope examples change held-out rejection differently from retrieved ones (rejection(random) - rejection(retrieval) != 0)
H2_relevance.prediction_stated_in_advance: if the acceptance shift comes from the presence of in-domain examples, the difference is near 0; if it comes from their relevance, random examples leave rejection higher. Both outcomes are reported with the fixed sentences below.

H3_rule_position.statement: repeating the scope rule after the examples raises held-out rejection relative to retrieval

H4_option_count.statement: on CLINC single-domain, the retrieval-minus-zero-shot change in held-out rejection differs between the 20-option and the 10-option prompts (difference of differences, paired on items)
H4_option_count.prediction_stated_in_advance: if option count drives the BANKING77-OOS effect, the 20-option change is more negative than the 10-option change

hypotheses.tests: paired sign-flip tests of per-item differences, clustered by held-out intent for rejection and by in-scope intent for in-scope measures, 10,000 draws; 95% cluster-bootstrap intervals
hypotheses.mechanism_measures: for every arm and model: held-out rejected, in-scope kept, in-scope right; for the general models d' and c (equal-variance signal detection, labelled as such, with the zROC-slope sensitivity of R1); for Jev AUROC of the scope probability and mean probability on held-out and in-scope items

outcome_sentences.H1 replicates: On fresh label-clean BANKING77-OOS items with a clean pool, retrieval lowers rejection of unsupported same-domain requests for {k} of 5 models by {range} points.
outcome_sentences.H1 fails: On fresh label-clean items with a clean pool the acceptance shift replicates for only {k} of 5 models; the run D result on BANKING77-OOS depended on its items or pool.
outcome_sentences.H2 near zero: Random in-scope examples shift the models as much as retrieved ones: the presence of in-domain examples, not their relevance, moves the decision towards acceptance.
outcome_sentences.H2 random higher: Random examples shift the models less than retrieved ones: relevant examples drive the acceptance shift.
outcome_sentences.H3 significant: Restating the scope rule after the examples recovers {d} points of rejection: part of the shift comes from separating the rule from the query.
outcome_sentences.H3 not significant: Restating the scope rule after the examples does not restore rejection.
outcome_sentences.H4 significant as predicted: Doubling the options on CLINC single-domain makes retrieval lower rejection: option count contributes to the difference between the splits.
outcome_sentences.H4 not significant: Doubling the options does not change retrieval's effect on CLINC single-domain; option count up to 20 does not explain the difference between the splits.
